lines: Every ride, click, and payment at Uber, Netflix, and LinkedIn becomes an event.
Kafka moves millions of them every second. Here's how.
Without it, every service talks directly to every other service. Add one more, and the wiring becomes a mess.
With Kafka, producers just write events to a topic: an append-only log. Each event gets a number, called an offset.
To scale, a topic is split into partitions, spread across servers called brokers, so writes happen in parallel.
Consumers read from the log at their own pace. In a consumer group, each one takes its own partitions, to share the work.
And events aren't deleted when they're read. They're stored and copied to other brokers, so if a server dies, nothing is lost, and you can replay the past.
Write once. Read by many. That's Kafka.
